mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where this trigger is met, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) that falls below 5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during these episodes, or the trigger fails to precede negative returns in at least 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of 1% or more over two consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered instances, or the median return is not statistically different from zero.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline of at least 1% in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based weakening in demand drivers, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall ≥1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4.5% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) is rising at an annualized rate above 3%, the combination signals a high-inflation, high-rate environment that erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative in these regimes, or the trigger is not followed by negative returns in at least 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase of at least 0.4 percentage points in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is a persistent signal of deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises ≥0.4pp in a single month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the median return is not significantly below zero.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of at least 2% over three consecutive months signals a sharp contraction in consumer demand, which directly reduces sales for retailers and input-sensitive firms, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during these episodes, or the trigger fails to precede negative returns in at least 40% of cases.
